intro: Google Docs on a Mac runs in your browser, so you work in Chrome, Edge or Safari. For technical writing, it handles headings, tables of contents, comments and templates well. It is weaker on section locking, content reuse and very long files, so plan around those limits from the start.
tldr: Use Chrome or Edge if you need offline work. Google lists offline access for those two browsers only.
Learn ⌘ / first. It opens the shortcut list in your own build, which beats any blog's list of keys.
Build procedure templates with File > New > From a template. Some template features need a work or school account.
Plan for the limits: 1.02 million characters per Doc, 40 named versions, and whole-version restore only.
Ask Lazur with ⌥ ⌘ for help on screen, or hold fn to dictate text at your cursor.

blocks.text: Technical writers spend a day inside one document. You write procedures, paste commands, reuse the same warning in several places and wait for engineers to comment. Google Docs covers most of that. It runs in any browser on your Mac, and version history keeps earlier copies.
What Google Docs does well for technical writing on Mac

Google Docs suits technical writing when your team already works in Google Workspace. Engineers can comment without installing anything. You keep one file as the working copy. The plainness helps when a procedure must stay readable under deadline.

The tool is weaker at structure. Docs does not lock sections, does not reuse content across files and has no topic model. Paligo, a documentation software vendor, makes these points in an article on managing technical documentation. Treat it as a vendor view, not a neutral test.

No public survey I could find measures how many technical writers use Google Docs. The closest data is old. A 2018 Tech Comm Census summary found 76% of respondents used Microsoft Word or Google Docs, combined. That number does not separate the two tools.
Set up Google Docs on your Mac before you write

Pick one browser and stick with it for documentation. Google's offline help names Chrome and Edge, and Safari is not on that list. Set up the browser before a big project starts, not during a deadline.

items: Install Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge, then open docs.google.com.
Create a separate Chrome profile for each Google account you use for work.
Install the Google Docs Offline Chrome extension if you need offline editing.
Open a Doc and press ⌘ / to check the shortcut list on your build.

blocks.text: Two details catch people out. Offline access is on by default when Drive for desktop is installed. Your admin can also turn it off for an account. If the offline option is missing, ask whoever manages your Workspace.
Keyboard shortcuts for technical writers in Google Docs

Shortcuts save more time than most writers expect. Google lists ⌘ B for bold and ⌘ ⌥ 1 through ⌘ ⌥ 6 for heading styles. You can set a heading without leaving the keyboard, which helps when you draft steps fast.

rows: Open a menu from the keyboard
blocks.caption: Shortcuts from Google's keyboard help page. Confirm them in your own build.

blocks.title: Shortcut lists disagree
blocks.text: Some guides list different keys for Tool finder. Google's own page gives two options for that command. Press ⌘ / in your Doc and trust what you see on your screen.

Menu access keys help when your hand stays on the keyboard. Google's help says Mac menu access uses Ctrl and Option, plus the underlined letter in the menu name. Try it on the File menu first, then learn the two menus you use most.
Headings, steps and tables of contents for procedures
A procedure needs three things: clear headings, numbered steps and a table of contents. Docs handles all three. You have to set them up on purpose, though, or the outline stays empty.

items: Type the procedure title and set it with Format > Paragraph styles > Title.
Set each main section to Heading 2 with ⌘ ⌥ 2, such as Prerequisites or Steps.
Type each step as a verb, such as Open, Select or Click, and use the numbered list button in the toolbar.
Choose Insert > Table of contents. Docs builds the outline from your heading styles.
After big changes, delete the table and insert it again so the entries refresh.

blocks.text: The common mistake is bold text used as a heading. Bold does not appear in the table of contents. Heading styles do, so the outline stays empty when writers skip them.
Templates for release notes and procedures in Google Docs
A template saves you from rebuilding the same frame for every release. Open the Template Gallery with File > New > From a template. Choose a template, then click Insert.
If the Doc already has content, the template opens in new document tabs instead. Work in a blank Doc when you want the template to fill it. Check the tab bar after you click Insert.

Some template features work only for work or school accounts. Google says @gmail.com accounts do not have access to them. Check which account you are signed in with before you build a library around one.
Google's help does not describe making your own template. The workaround is File > Make a copy. Build a clean release note Doc, name it Release notes template, and copy it for each release.

items: Title and version line, set in the Title and Heading 2 styles.
Date, owner and status, as plain paragraphs.
New, Changed, Fixed and Known issues, each set as Heading 2.
Placeholder text in square brackets, so nobody forgets to replace it.

blocks.text: Keep the template free of live numbers and names. Otherwise the next writer copies last month's details by mistake. A placeholder is safer than a stale value.
Version history, comments and suggesting mode for review
Version history is your safety net. Open File > Version history > See version history. Each entry shows the time and the editors, and you can name a version to find it later.

Restore works on whole versions. Google's help describes restoring an earlier version or making a copy from it. It does not describe undoing one change. To get one sentence back, open the old version, copy the sentence and paste it into the current file.
Named versions have a cap. A Google Doc can hold up to 40 named versions. Name the ones you need for review, such as Sent to engineering, and skip naming every save.
Paligo says restoring a version can overwrite other writers' work. That is a vendor claim, but the risk is real for any whole-version restore. Ask your team to name a version before anyone restores.
Use comments for review questions. Use suggesting mode for small edits. The mode switch sits near the Share button. Suggested edits appear as changes that an engineer can accept or reject.
Markdown files and code samples in Google Docs

Google announced on October 5, 2026 that you can open, edit and collaborate on .md and .markdown files in Docs without converting them. Drive shows rendered previews. Google says the rollout is gradual on Workspace Rapid and Scheduled Release domains, and it can take up to 15 days to reach all users.
Test one file before you move a docs folder. The announcement lists no technical limits. Check how headings, tables, code blocks and links survive a round trip, and compare them with the source file.

Code samples in plain Docs take a workaround. Put each sample in a one-cell table with a light gray background, then set a monospaced font such as Courier New. Keep samples short so readers can copy them cleanly.
Offline work, file limits and large documents

Docs has a hard size cap. A Google Doc can hold up to 1.02 million characters. A long manual can reach that cap sooner than you expect. Split it by chapter early, with one Doc per chapter and an index Doc that links them.

Google's Drive limits page gives a different number for converted files. A text document converted to Docs format can be up to 50 MB. The page gives no separate limit for .doc or .docx files, so test your largest file before a migration.

Offline editing has strict rules. You need Chrome or Edge with the Google Docs Offline extension. Private and incognito windows do not work. Only one account per browser profile can have offline access enabled.

items: Open the Doc in Chrome or Edge, and confirm offline access is on.
Turn Wi-Fi off from the menu bar.
Type one sentence and close the tab.
Turn Wi-Fi back on, reopen the Doc and check that the sentence saved.

blocks.text: Chrome, Edge and Safari on your Mac: which to use

Safari is common on Macs, but Google's offline help names only Chrome and Edge. Use one of those when you need offline work. For plain online editing, any of the three works, so choose the one you already trust.

Memory use is a real complaint. One Apple Developer Forums thread from 2024 reports Google Docs and Sheets using 4 to 5 GB of RAM in Safari, versus 1 to 2 GB in Chrome. The poster gave no macOS or browser versions. Treat it as one report and test on your own Mac.
To test it yourself, open Activity Monitor from Applications > Utilities. Sort by Memory, open the same Doc in each browser, and compare the browser rows after a few minutes of typing.
Where Google Docs gets in the way for documentation teams
Teams hit the same friction points again and again. Paligo says Google Docs has no way to lock sections or prevent conflicting edits. It also says reuse means copying content into each channel.
Translation adds work. Paligo says each language needs its own copy, and the full document is resent after every change. That is a vendor view. Plan for it if you localize.

AI is already part of the workflow. In the 2026 State of Docs survey, 76% of respondents use AI regularly for documentation creation. Among technical writers, 31% report saving 50% or more of their time, against 35% of all respondents.
A DrExplain summary of the same survey lists outdated screenshots, jargon and navigation problems. It gives no percentages and does not mention Google Docs. The tool is one factor among several.
Using Lazur with Google Docs on your Mac

Lazur runs alongside your browser, so you can ask about the Doc on screen. Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask your question. Lazur answers out loud. Ask where a control is and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it.
Ask how to do something and Lazur guides you one click at a time. It waits for each click before it moves on. Lazur does not click for you, and it is not a plugin or add-in for Google Docs.
Hold fn to dictate. Clean, formatted text lands at your cursor in any app. A personal dictionary helps with product names, command flags and internal terms that you spell the same way every time.

Privacy works like this. Lazur listens and looks at your screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models.
Pricing and the trial are on the [pricing page](/pricing). If you already draft in Google Docs on your Mac, read the [Google Docs assistant page](/apps/google-docs) for the full feature list.
Common mistakes technical writers make in Google Docs

items: Using bold instead of heading styles, which keeps headings out of the table of contents.
Copying one procedure into several Docs, so the edits drift apart. Keep one source and link to it.
Restoring an old version to fix one sentence, which can roll back other people's work.
Trusting a shortcut from a blog without pressing ⌘ / in your own build.
Ignoring the character cap until a long manual is close to it.
Building a template library on a @gmail.com account, then missing features that need a work or school account.

blocks.text: Most of these come from working fast. A short check on setup, browser and file size saves rework later. Do that check at the start of each project, not at the end.
What to do next with Google Docs on your Mac

Start with one real procedure. Set the heading styles, build a release note template and insert a table of contents. Then test offline access and your largest file. Do those checks before a big project starts.
Keep your own shortcut list in a Doc named Shortcuts. Add each key the first time you need it. When you forget one, hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask Lazur to explain it.

If your team uses Microsoft tools, read [Word for technical writers on Mac](/for/technical-writers/word). For dictation setup in Chrome, read the [Google Docs voice typing guide](/blog/google-docs-voice-typing-mac). To check your typing speed, try the [typing speed test](/tools/typing-speed-test).

faq.question: Does Google Docs work offline on a Mac?
faq.answer: Yes, in Chrome or Edge. Install the Google Docs Offline Chrome extension and turn offline access on. Private and incognito windows do not work. Only one account per browser profile can have offline enabled, and admins can turn it off for an account.

faq.question: What is the Google Docs character limit?
faq.answer: A Google Doc can hold up to 1.02 million characters. Google's Drive limits page says a text document converted to Docs format can be up to 50 MB. The page gives no separate limit for .doc or .docx files, so test your largest file first.

faq.question: How do I make a table of contents in Google Docs on Mac?
faq.answer: Apply heading styles first, with Format > Paragraph styles or ⌘ ⌥ 1 through ⌘ ⌥ 6. Then choose Insert > Table of contents and pick a style. Bold text does not count as a heading, so the outline stays empty if you skip the styles.

faq.question: Can I restore one sentence from an old version?
faq.answer: Not directly. Version history restores whole versions, and Google's help does not describe reverting a single change. Open the old version, copy the sentence, then paste it into the current file.

faq.question: Why does Google Docs use so much memory in Safari?
faq.answer: One 2024 Apple Developer Forums thread reports 4 to 5 GB of RAM in Safari, versus 1 to 2 GB in Chrome. The poster gave no macOS or browser versions. Compare the two browsers on your own Mac in Activity Monitor.

faq.question: Can I open Markdown files in Google Docs?
faq.answer: Google announced on October 5, 2026 that .md and .markdown files can be opened and edited in Docs without conversion. The rollout is gradual on Workspace Rapid and Scheduled Release domains and can take up to 15 days. Test one file before you move a folder.

faq.question: Can Lazur type into Google Docs for me?
faq.answer: Lazur drafts text and dictation puts text at your cursor when you hold fn. Lazur does not click buttons or operate apps for you. You still place the cursor and confirm each change in the Doc yourself.

faq.question: Is Google Docs good for technical writing?
faq.answer: For small teams with simple documents, yes. It handles headings, tables of contents, comments and templates well. It lacks section locking and content reuse, so larger documentation sets may need a dedicated tool, according to a documentation vendor's review.
